image_description: A close-up, rear-angle view of a male duck (drake) floating on water. The image focuses on the tail and hindquarters, showing brown speckled flank feathers, a grey vent area, and the characteristic curled black central tail feathers. A patch of white and iridescent blue speculum feathers is visible on the wing. The head is partially visible on the far left but mostly out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head and bill are largely outside the frame or obscured by the angle; only the back of the neck/head is barely visible.
The eyes are not visible in this rear-facing crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the head color is missing, the body displays complex male-specific patterning: rich brown speckling on the flanks, a distinct grey vent area, and the presence of the bright blue speculum patch on the wing, which confirms it is not a plain female plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the signature upward-curling black central tail feathers, a definitive anatomical trait of a drake.
